cards.text: Selected compounds in the amide-bioisostere series were reported not to degrade GSPT1 or IKZF1. The body directs readers to supplementary Table S1 and Figure S5; the sentence does not enumerate every selected compound or its individual conditions. Keep this as a group statement.
cards.coverage_reason: Generic extraction has individual GSPT1 and IKZF1 rows with >10000 nM bounds. No claim of a wholly new negative result.

cards.text: Compounds 5 and 6 bind CRBN similarly (FP 1.3 and 1.4 uM), yet CK1alpha Dmax falls from 82% to 23%; IKZF1 Dmax falls from 84% to 57%. HiBiT CK1alpha uses HEK293 and IKZF1 uses Jurkat cells. Dmax is maximum degradation over 24 h at 10 uM. NanoBRET complex formation is a separate 2 h experiment. Compound 6 is weaker, not non-binding or an exact zero.
cards.coverage_reason: Both resources contain degradation; MolGlueDB includes binding and time. Useful only as endpoint/context control.

cards.text: Benzimidazole compound 20 was reported inactive up to 10 uM in degradation and antiproliferation assays. The sentence supplies no exact measured Dmax. Compound 21 instead has CK1alpha DC50 0.004 uM (4 nM), Dmax 89%, antiproliferation IC50 0.022 uM. Initial endpoint CK1alpha HiBiT screening of this series was at 24 h; MOLM-13 antiproliferation at 72 h. Potent compounds subsequently received kinetic profiling.
cards.coverage_reason: MolGlueDB contains compound20 Dmax=0 and compound21 DC50=2 nM; narrative gives qualitative20 and endpoint21=4 nM. Different assay/curation representations are not automatically errors.

cards.text: LC-02-105 induces CK1alpha degradation in MOLM13; GSPT1 is spared and IKZF2 effects are minimal. Figure1C immunoblots used24h treatment, with concentrations not enumerated in the caption text. WEE1 was not detected; authors suggest low basal expression. This does not establish that the compound cannot degrade measurable WEE1.

cards.text: dCK1alpha-1 degrades CK1alpha in wild-type cells but spares CRBN-null cells. The body names MOLM13 for the null comparison, while Figure3C caption names MOLT4 parental/CRBN-null cells and 6h. This cell-line discrepancy remains unresolved. Separately, Figure3D specifies MOLM13 pretreatment 1h with MLN4924, bortezomib or pomalidomide followed by 100nM degrader 6h; these treatments rescue degradation. In MOLM13, 100nM causes degradation from 2h through at least 24h. Do not merge these separate assays.
cards.coverage_reason: No CRBN-null/rescue records in the source-filtered exports; retain source cell-line discrepancy.

cards.text: dCK1alpha-1 combined with navtemadlin (AMG-232) shows antiproliferative synergy in MOLM13 over3days, evaluated with HSA. No significant combinatorial effect was observed in DLD-1, T98G or HEK293T. This is a combination/viability endpoint, not evidence that either compound has zero degradation or no individual activity. Exact doses for those negative cell lines are not given in the body passage.
cards.coverage_reason: Both exports omit combination-response boundaries. Auxiliary phenotype, not a direct degradation failure.

cards.text: SJ0040 and SJ3149 show IKZF1 Dmax <10% in Jurkat HiBiT. Here Dmax is maximum over 24h at 10uM; DC50 is measured at 4h. SJ3149 is not devoid of IKZF2 effects: MOLM13 WB 4h shows ~40% IKZF2 reduction at 10uM, while CK1alpha reaches 50% degradation at 4nM. Keep cell, protein, time and dose separate.

cards.text: SJ0040 and SJ3149 do not affect CK1alpha levels in CRBN-knockout MOLM13 as reported in Supplementary Fig1c,d; exact degradation conditions are not specified in that body statement. For viability, WT and CRBN-null MOLM13 were treated with 1uM SJ7095, SJ0040 or SJ3149 at 24/72h; at 72h WT death increases (~80% dead/dying for SJ3149), but CRBN-null viability is unaffected. A separate G40N CK1alpha overexpression experiment in MOLM13 confirms degradation resistance and reduced 72h viability response, not necessarily zero cytotoxicity.
cards.coverage_reason: No CRBN-knockout or G40N experimental boundary in either source-filtered export.

cards.text: Lenalidomide did not show appreciable cytotoxicity in MOLM13 even at high concentrations. This does not mean inability to degrade CK1alpha: 100uM for 24h gave a degradation effect comparable to 100nM SJ7095 for 4h in MOLM13 WB. The screening viability endpoint is 72h CellTiterGlo. Protein removal and cell death are separate endpoints.

cards.text: 6- and 7-substituted Len cores are generally inactive in degradation despite retaining CRBN binding. The tested G-loop neosubstrates are IKZF3, CK1alpha, GSPT1, SALL4. The authors propose failure to form a productive ternary complex as an explanation; this is not a direct measurement proving zero complex formation. Four of 24 compounds had CRBN binding IC50 >10uM. Ymin 100%=no protein reduction, 0%=complete degradation.

cards.text: For GSPT1, 16a has EC50 >10uM, Ymin 100%; 22a has EC50 1.4uM, Ymin 2.3%. Ymin is remaining protein, not percent degraded, so 22a induces much deeper degradation. For IKZF3, 13a EC50 1.86uM, Ymin 79%; 19a EC50 0.012uM, Ymin 9.2%. These are tested endpoint-specific results, not all proteins.

cards.text: Figure3g comparison tested UDP-glucose, UDP-NAG, UDP-galactose and IMiDs thalidomide, lenalidomide, pomalidomide for glucokinase degradation. Only UDP-glucose was reported to induce glucokinase degradation among those compounds. This is a group-level tested comparison; the body passage does not list dose, time, cell line for each negative arm. It does not establish universal IMiD inactivity.

In pancreatic NIT-1 cells, the paper reports UDP-glucose dose-dependent endogenous glucokinase protein reduction and a degradation time course 3–72h. Glucokinase transcription was unchanged over that period. Unchanged RNA is not absence of protein reduction. No exact DC50 or Dmax is given in this body passage.

The paper reports WB glucokinase protein reduction after 10mM UDP-glucose in HEK293 and 1mM in NCI-H929-1a. Intracellular UDP-glucose was comparatively high in HEK293 and low in NCI-H929-1a. These are administered concentration examples, not measured DC50 values or universal minimum thresholds.
